Workflow configuration selects agents as assignments from the shared profile library: one implementer assignment per context, and an ordered cohort of specialist validator assignments with stable use-site identity. A cohort reviews one frozen candidate deterministically — all required validators must pass the same candidate, the cohort charges one validation iteration per semantic round regardless of validator count, findings stay grouped by assignment, and infrastructure failures never masquerade as review verdicts. Validators become mechanically read-only. Prompt authority is enforced at the transport level for task-strategy validation, with the role contract dominant over user-authored profile text. Existing persisted configuration migrates once, with hard cutover.
conventions: Implement only the task and criterion contract in the current lane context pack.
Treat approved validation strategy notes as the boundary of validator judgment.
nonGoals: Non-goals: Multiple implementers editing one context (multi-implementer coordination overlaps later roadmap work; one implementer per context stands). Advisory non-gating validators (required-only in v1; advisory is a later explicit mode if evidence demands it). Migrating the D1 plan-repair agent onto the library (future consumer; its evidence integration here is read-only). Any inbound compatibility parser for legacy singleton config shapes (locked: hard cutover). Agent-planned lane assignment and same-worktree parallelism (roadmap D5). New mutation paths outside the existing live-edit choke point. Field-merging profiles across cascade tiers — assignments replace as whole units.
Work excluded from the pinned execution scope.

invariants.statement: Locked by Alex 2026-08-01 via the ticket #39 collaboration, as amended by Alex 2026-08-03 during requirements review: (1) one-time migration of persisted implementer/validator config onto built-in profile assignments, hard cutover, no inbound compatibility parser; the archived-execution-blob read-path decode floor is APPROVED (Alex 2026-08-03) as the single recorded backward-compatibility exception — archived blobs keep a read-only legacy decoder and are never rewritten; (2) cutover requires terminal executions: the migration auto-aborts any non-terminal execution with a distinct migration-cutover abort reason surfaced in the inspector, and no live runtime state (working definitions, lane keys, continuity, pending questions) is migrated (Alex 2026-08-03); (3) assignments are replaced whole at cascade boundaries (global -> workflow -> context), never field-merged; (4) a semantic cohort failure charges exactly one validation iteration and one consecutive-failure count; (5) validators are mechanically read-only via a backend-enforced write-restriction envelope with an explicit per-lane write allowlist — this supersedes the 2026-08-01 detect-restore-and-bound mutation handling, which is dropped along with mutation incidents, bounds, and the mutation halt kind (Alex 2026-08-03); (6) profile text enters task-strategy validation through executeWorkflowTaskRun.systemInstructions via the companion spec's composer, extended here with the single focus-aware interface, role contract dominant, with adversarial-profile and adversarial-focus tests on both backends; (7) the seeded default remains a single general-reviewer assignment so existing workflows keep one reviewer invocation per round; (8) dynamic mutation rides the doc 05/06 live-edit surface (pause-to-edit for started contexts) — no new choke points; (9) validator questions are per-lane: multiple validators in one context may park questions simultaneously, surfaced together in Needs You, and a lane awaiting an answer is an unsettled round outcome — this supersedes the per-context question mutex (Alex 2026-08-03); (10) cohort parallelism is subordinate to the engine's existing global query budget (Alex 2026-08-03). Implementation prerequisite: this spec's implementation does not start until the agent-profile-library spec's library service, snapshot contract (including renderedInstructionBlock), and composer are merged — the governing charter and roadmap D3 wording must be amended to record this dependency (D3 is two sequenced specs, no longer 'independent of everything else'). Engineering contract per AGENTS.md: workflow modules per the adoption matrix, publication seam for events, round-trip contract tests for persisted shapes, full repository suite green at the published tip before closeout.

Approved task workflow-validator-cohorts/T16

Red-green TDD. Second round task: on script success dispatch every specialist simultaneously (Promise.all over per-assignment lanes); admission governed solely by the existing global query semaphore — introduce a TYPED pre-admission classification (e.g. a distinct queue-admission-timeout error from the dispatch path) so a semaphore admission timeout is queue pressure that does NOT consume a specialist attempt; attempts (3 total per specialist per round, persisted) count only admitted dispatches that then fail as infrastructure. Retry only the affected specialist against the unchanged candidate with sibling verdicts retained. Conclusion precedence per the amended R6: once every non-infra-failed specialist reports, any semantic rejection concludes semantically — exactly ONE consecutiveFailureCount increment and one reopen mutation grouped by assignment with task-ID-only dedup (infra-failed specialists rerun next round); all pass resets the counter; no rejection + an exhausted required specialist leaves the round UNCONCLUDED and uncharged — settled verdicts retained, no aggregate event — and halts the context with validator_infra_error extended additively { assignmentId, attempts, roundSeq }; resume resets that round's attempt counters, re-verifies the candidate, and reruns only unsettled specialists. Prove: plan-repair trigger untouched by infra halts; budget-below-cohort-size FIFO admission with no cohort-internal ordering; an artificially slow specialist never delays a sibling's start; no specialist launches before script success; aggregate assembly in configured cohort order; circuit-breaker accounting identical to a single-validator failure (R5.2); lifecycle-classifier resumability for the extended halt.

Narrow context pack
Requirements:
- workflow-validator-cohorts/R5: A validation round shall be deterministic: (1) a persisted round/candidate identity freezes with the validator roster at round start, before any validator runs; the identity covers the candidate's tracked content (diff scope) and task-state generation — ignored build artifacts and lane logs are outside it — and the implementer cannot run while the cohort owns the candidate; (2) the script validator runs first against the frozen candidate, its outputs and logs are written outside the candidate's tracked tree, and after the script phase the engine re-verifies the candidate identity — a mismatch concludes the round as an infrastructure outcome, never a semantic verdict; (3) a deterministic script failure short-circuits the round with zero specialists launched; only after script success are the cohort specialists admitted, all concurrently, per the validator-parallelism requirement; (4) every specialist receives byte-identical common inputs — charter, invariants, acceptance criteria, task state, diff scope — differing only in its own rendered profile block; (5) remediation begins only when the round has concluded per the infrastructure requirement's rules — every specialist settled by semantic verdict or infrastructure exhaustion, or a mixed round concluded on a semantic rejection with infra-failed specialists deferred to the next round; findings stay grouped by assignment, only reopened task IDs are deduplicated, and a result arriving for a stale candidate identity is rejected, never recorded; (6) any required-validator semantic failure fails the cohort, the implementer receives all findings in one remediation pass, and the cohort charges exactly one validation iteration and one consecutive-failure count.
- workflow-validator-cohorts/R16: Within a validation round, the specialist phase shall have no cohort-internal ordering: once the script validator passes against the frozen candidate, every specialist assignment is admitted for launch immediately, and no specialist's start shall wait on a sibling specialist's completion or verdict. On a deterministic script failure zero specialists launch. Actual starts are governed solely by the engine's existing global concurrency budget (maxConcurrentQueries) — the cohort introduces no additional serialization of its own. Aggregate results are assembled in configured cohort order, never completion order.
- workflow-validator-cohorts/R6: An infrastructure failure (provider error, timeout, malformed output after structured-output repair) shall not be a review verdict: only the affected specialist retries against the unchanged frozen candidate, other specialists' collected verdicts are retained for that round, no implementation task reopens, and no validation iteration is charged. Infrastructure attempts are fixed at 3 total per specialist per round in v1 — one initial attempt plus two retries, no per-cohort configuration — with the attempt count persisted; exhaustion halts the context with an infrastructure halt kind (repairable/resumable — resuming the halt resets that round's attempt counters), and infrastructure halts are never plan-repair triggers. Mixed rounds have defined precedence: once every non-infra-failed specialist has reported, any semantic rejection concludes the round as a semantic failure (one iteration charge, remediation proceeds, the infra-failed specialists simply rerun in the next round); a round left with only infrastructure outcomes does not conclude — it remains open and uncharged with its settled verdicts retained, publishes no aggregate verdict, and specialist exhaustion halts the context resumably as above. Event semantics: the aggregate cohort validation-result event is published only for semantically concluded rounds and remains the sole evidence-ingestion record; infrastructure failures, stale-result rejections, and partial rounds publish distinct non-verdict event kinds that evidence ingestion ignores.
Approved decisions:
- workflow-validator-cohorts/D4: A persisted validationRound freezes the exact reviewed tree and roster; specialists run concurrently against it
  Chosen approach: Context state gains validationRound (runtime tier, nullable): { seq (monotonic per context), candidate: { headSha, candidateTreeHash, taskStateHash }, roster: [{ assignmentId, profileRef, revision, resolvedInstructionHash, strategy }], specialists: per-assignment { state: pending|running|verdict_pass|verdict_fail|infra_failed|parked, attempts, summary?, issues?, questionToken? }, phase, startedAt } — bounded by cohort size. The round freezes at round start, before any validator runs. Candidate identity covers exactly what validators review: candidateTreeHash is the git tree hash written from the same TEMPORARY INDEX the diff pipeline already builds (src/lib/git/diff.ts stages untracked files into a temp index precisely so they appear in the rendered diff), so untracked content and file-mode changes are inside the identity, while gitignored build artifacts and lane logs remain outside it; headSha pins the base and taskStateHash covers the context's task tuples. The implementer cannot run while the round is open: the engine's existing within-context serialization already guarantees it, and the seed path adds an explicit refusal while validationRound is non-null as a structural guard. The script validator keeps its existing script-first position (processContextCompletionValidation runs processScriptValidation before any agent validation) and its existing worktree log location (.cc/workflow/ is gitignored, hence outside the identity — pinned by test); a deterministic script failure short-circuits with zero specialists launched and keeps its existing remediation-task accounting. - workflow-validator-cohorts/D15: Simultaneous specialist dispatch, admission by the existing global semaphore, aggregation in cohort order
  Chosen approach: Once the script validator passes against the frozen candidate, the round dispatches every specialist assignment immediately (Promise.all over per-assignment runs); no specialist's start waits on a sibling's completion or verdict, and on a deterministic script failure zero specialists launch. - workflow-validator-cohorts/D5: Fixed 3 post-admission attempts per specialist; exhaustion halts resumably with verdicts retained; incidents are never verdicts
  Chosen approach: Infrastructure outcomes (provider error, timeout, post-repair malformed output — today's infra_error reasons) never become verdicts: only the affected specialist retries against the unchanged frozen candidate, sibling verdicts already recorded in the round stand, no task reopens, and no iteration or failure count is charged. Live proof task; use cctl dev ensure + the cc-live-feature-test skill; confirm backend state (SQLite rows, events, transcripts), not the UI alone. The implementer at every cascade level shall become an AgentAssignment, and cascade resolution (global -> workflow -> context) shall replace the whole assignment at each override boundary — never merge fields across tiers.
Approved decisions:
- workflow-validator-cohorts/D4: A persisted validationRound freezes the exact reviewed tree and roster; specialists run concurrently against it
  Chosen approach: Context state gains validationRound (runtime tier, nullable): { seq (monotonic per context), candidate: { headSha, candidateTreeHash, taskStateHash }, roster: [{ assignmentId, profileRef, revision, resolvedInstructionHash, strategy }], specialists: per-assignment { state: pending|running|verdict_pass|verdict_fail|infra_failed|parked, attempts, summary?, issues?, questionToken? }, phase, startedAt } — bounded by cohort size. The round freezes at round start, before any validator runs. Candidate identity covers exactly what validators review: candidateTreeHash is the git tree hash written from the same TEMPORARY INDEX the diff pipeline already builds (src/lib/git/diff.ts stages untracked files into a temp index precisely so they appear in the rendered diff), so untracked content and file-mode changes are inside the identity, while gitignored build artifacts and lane logs remain outside it; headSha pins the base and taskStateHash covers the context's task tuples. The implementer cannot run while the round is open: the engine's existing within-context serialization already guarantees it, and the seed path adds an explicit refusal while validationRound is non-null as a structural guard. The script validator keeps its existing script-first position (processContextCompletionValidation runs processScriptValidation before any agent validation) and its existing worktree log location (.cc/workflow/ is gitignored, hence outside the identity — pinned by test); a deterministic script failure short-circuits with zero specialists launched and keeps its existing remediation-task accounting. The engine recomputes the candidate identity at three points: after the script phase (a mismatch concludes the round as an infrastructure outcome — non-verdict event, no charge, no specialists), before accepting each specialist result (a result carrying a stale (seq, candidate) pair is rejected as an incident, never recorded), and before publishing the aggregate result.   Chosen approach: The companion composer gains the one focus-aware interface this spec adds: composeProfileBlock(profile, options?: { assignmentFocus?: string }) and buildAgentProfileSnapshot(profile, options?) in src/lib/agent-profiles/composer.ts. Workflow lane creation is a pre-resolved-snapshot handoff: the lane conversation persists and injects exactly the execution-seeded snapshot and rendered block — no re-resolution, no Standard Agent default, no second profile injection — so a delayed lane can neither pick up a newer revision nor fail on a post-seed deletion. Lanes replay the stored block byte-identically across restarts and composer upgrades. Later library edits or deletions shall not affect the execution. Definition acceptance and workflow validate shall fail closed on dangling references, and execution start shall re-check before seeding. Global defaults and global templates shall be refused when referencing project-tier profiles; project definitions may reference all tiers.
- workflow-validator-cohorts/R10: Workflow roles shall receive composed instructions from the neutral composer through their actual transports: conversation-backed lanes via session/runtime instructions and task-strategy validation via executeWorkflowTaskRun.systemInstructions. User-authored profile text shall never be placed alone at system priority above the role contract: composition puts the role harness, scope rules, and verdict/output schema first at the authoritative layer, with the profile as a delimited subordinate lens, delivered through the strongest privileged instruction channel the backend offers for that transport (Claude's system-prompt channel; Codex developer/system instructions where available — never solely inline user-prompt text when a privileged channel exists), and permissions and output schemas enforced externally.
